mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 4% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent drop in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its previous 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings prospects and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such INDPRO weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months indicates a broad-based demand contraction, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above the previous 12-month average for two consecutive months, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for 2 consecutive months AND UNRATE stable
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such labor market expansion signals.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% annualized for three consecutive months, coupled with stable federal funds rates, signals inflationary pressure without monetary tightening, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% annualized for 3 months AND FEDFUNDS unchanged
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative under such inflationary but stable-rate conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months, without a corresponding rise in consumption (GDPC1), signals a savings glut that depresses aggregate demand and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for 4 months AND GDPC1 flat or declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is persistently above its moving average and GDPC1 is flat or declining.
